issues.failure_explanation: The equivalence of (1.1) and (1.2) is asserted by exhibiting the Brownian-bridge feedback control $\bar\theta$ as an element of $\Theta$. But $\mathbb E\int_0^1|\bar\theta_t|^2dt=\int_0^1(\mathbb E|x_0-\xi|^2+dt/(1-t))dt=\infty$ (the paper's own computation of $I_2$ shows the energy over $[0,1-\delta]$ grows like $d\ln(1/\delta)$), so $\bar\theta\notin\Theta$ and the minimum in (1.2) is not attained by it. The paper only establishes (via truncated bridges in Theorem 2.3) that the infimum in (1.2) equals $\min G$, not that it is attained.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes only the operator-type estimate $\mathbb E|\delta Y_t|\le 2K_G\|\phi\|_{L^2}$ for the full directional derivative $\delta Y_t=\partial_x\partial_\mu\mathcal V_\eps(\xi)\phi(\xi)+\tilde{\mathbb E}[\partial^2_{\mu\mu}\mathcal V_\eps(\xi,\tilde\xi)\phi(\tilde\xi)]$. An $L^1$–$L^2$ bound on this map does not yield a pointwise bound on the kernel $\partial^2_{\mu\mu}\mathcal V_\eps(t,\mu)(x,y)$ for all $x,y$ (e.g. for atomic $\mu=\mu^N$ and $\phi$ supported on one atom of mass $1/N$, the estimate only controls $\frac1N|\partial_x\partial_\mu\mathcal V\,e+\frac1N\partial^2_{\mu\mu}\mathcal V(x_i,x_i)e|$ by $2K_G/\sqrt N$, which gives no uniform bound), yet exactly such pointwise bounds at atoms are what Assumption 3.1(b) and the appendix require. Likewise the pointwise bound $|\partial_x\partial_\mu\mathcal V_\eps|\le 2K_G$ is inferred from (eq:Y-Lcontinuity), an $L^1$ estimate for random initial data with different laws, without any argument passing to the decoupling field for fixed $\mu$. The intermediate a.s. claim $|\delta X_1|\le|\phi(\xi)|$ is also unjustified since only $\mathbb E[\delta X\cdot\delta Y]\ge0$ (not pathwise positivity) is available.

issues.failure_explanation: For $t<s$, comparing $\mathcal V_\eps(t,\mu)$ with $\mathcal V_\eps(s,\mu)$ via the dynamic programming principle involves $\mathcal V_\eps(s,\mathcal L(X^{t,\xi;\theta}_s))$, and $\mathcal L(X_s)\ne\mu$ because of the Brownian noise on $[t,s]$ (even for $\theta\equiv0$, $\mathcal L(X_s)=\mu*N(0,(s-t)I)$). diagnostic_evidence.quote: The expectation of the Wasserstein distance $\E[\mathcal W_2(\mu^N_{\mathbf{X}}, \mu)]$ converges to zero as $N$  tends to infinity but with the rate depending on the dimension $d$ and the moments of $\mu$.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims $\mathbb E[\mathcal W_2(\mu^N_{\mathbf X},\mu)]\le C_\alpha N^{-1/2-\alpha}$ for every $\alpha>0$ when $d\le4$, i.e. a rate faster than $N^{-1/2}$. This is false: for $d=1$ and $\mu=\frac12(\delta_0+\delta_1)$, $\mathcal W_2(\mu^N,\mu)^2=|p_N-\frac12|$ with $p_N$ the empirical frequency, so $\mathbb E[\mathcal W_2]\asymp N^{-1/4}$. The known (Fournier–Guillin) bounds give $\mathbb E[\mathcal W_2^2]\lesssim N^{-1/2}$ for $d<4$ (with a log factor at $d=4$) and $N^{-2/d}$ for $d>4$, hence $\mathbb E[\mathcal W_2]\lesssim N^{-1/4}$ in low dimension, not $N^{-1/2-\alpha}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed rates by the correct ones, e.g. $\mathbb E[\mathcal W_2]\le C N^{-1/4}$ for $d<4$, $C(N^{-1/2}\ln(1+N))^{1/2}$ for $d=4$, $CN^{-1/d}$ for $d>4$.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative sampling-error rate advertised for Corollary 3.6 in low dimensions is overstated; the corollary itself (with the abstract term $\mathbb E[\mathcal W_2]$) is unaffected.
issues.title: Misstated empirical-measure Wasserstein rate ($N^{-1/2-\alpha}$ for $d\le4$) is impossible
issues.why_classification: Only a remark's quoted rate needs correction; no proof or theorem depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The exact drift (1.25)/(beta) is a ratio of expectations over the joint noise of all $N$ particles with weight $\exp(-\frac1\eps[\sum_j F(Y_{j,l})+\frac1{2N}\sum_{j,k}\Phi(Y_{j,l}-Y_{k,l})])$. The 'simplified' formula keeps only the terms involving $Y_{i,l}$, discarding $\sum_{j\ne i}F(Y_{j,l})+\frac1{2N}\sum_{j,k\ne i}\Phi(Y_{j,l}-Y_{k,l})$. These discarded terms vary with the sample index $l$ (they fluctuate by $O(\sqrt N)$ and are divided by $\eps$), so they do not cancel between numerator and denominator; 'independence of noises' yields cancellation only when $G$ has no interaction term, which is precisely the case excluded. Algorithm 2 instead freezes one draw $\tilde\mu_T$ of the other particles and computes a conditional ratio $\mathbb E[e^{-U/\eps}Y_i\,|\,\xi^{-i}]/\mathbb E[e^{-U/\eps}\,|\,\xi^{-i}]$, whose expectation is not the ratio of expectations in (1.25). Hence neither the simplified formula nor Algorithm 2 is a consistent ($S\to\infty$) estimator of the optimal drift they claim to approximate.
